title: Docs: Mention Vite publicDir interference

## What I did Short term fix for #24627 until the issue can be addressed, as it could involve breaking changes. ## Checklist for Contributors ### Testing N/A #### Manual testing N/A, docs. Visit http://localhost:3000/docs/api/main-config/main-config-static-dirs for outcome: ### Documentation N/A ## Checklist for Maintainers - [x] When this PR is ready for testing, make sure to add `ci:normal`, `ci:merged` or `ci:daily` GH label to it to run a specific set of sandboxes. The particular set of sandboxes can be found in `code/lib/cli-storybook/src/sandbox-templates.ts` - [x] Make sure this PR contains **one** of the labels below:
Available labels - `bug`: Internal changes that fixes incorrect behavior. - `maintenance`: User-facing maintenance tasks. - `dependencies`: Upgrading (sometimes downgrading) dependencies. - `build`: Internal-facing build tooling & test updates. Will not show up in release changelog. - `cleanup`: Minor cleanup style change. Will not show up in release changelog. - `documentation`: Documentation **only** changes. Will not show up in release changelog. - `feature request`: Introducing a new feature. - `BREAKING CHANGE`: Changes that break compatibility in some way with current major version. - `other`: Changes that don't fit in the above categories.
### 🦋 Canary release This PR does not have a canary release associated. You can request a canary release of this pull request by mentioning the `@storybookjs/core` team here. _core team members can create a canary release [here](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/actions/workflows/publish.yml) or locally with `gh workflow run --repo storybookjs/storybook publish.yml --field pr=`_ ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Documentation** * Clarified how Vite-based frameworks may copy extra static directories into build output and added informational callouts explaining this behavior. * Explained how to disable the behavior by setting Vite's publicDir to false, and preserved existing configuration guidance for static assets. ✏️ Tip: You can customize this high-level summary in your review settings.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

<details>
<summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>

🌐 Web query:

`Vite publicDir option documentation behavior`

💡 Result:

Summary — Vite publicDir behavior (concise)

- What it is: publicDir (type string | false, default "public") points to a directory of plain static assets. Files there are served at / during dev and copied as-is to the root of outDir during build. They are not transformed. ([v3.vitejs.dev](https://v3.vitejs.dev/config/shared-options.html?utm_source=openai))

- Config values: a path (absolute or relative to project root) or false to disable the feature. ([v3.vitejs.dev](https://v3.vitejs.dev/config/shared-options.html?utm_source=openai))

- Usage notes/quirk: public assets must be referenced with root-absolute paths (e.g. /favicon.ico). Also note that in dev mode Vite historically serves files from the project root as well (so files outside publicDir can be reachable in dev), which can mask missing/incorrect references and has been discussed in the Vite repo. ([v3.vitejs.dev](https://v3.vitejs.dev/guide/assets.html?utm_source=openai))

If you want specific examples or how to set publicDir in vite.config.ts, tell me which format (JS/TS) you use.

Citations:

- 1: https://v3.vitejs.dev/config/shared-options.html?utm_source=openai
- 2: https://v3.vitejs.dev/config/shared-options.html?utm_source=openai
- 3: https://v3.vitejs.dev/guide/assets.html?utm_source=openai

---

🌐 Web query:

`Vite static asset handling public directory`

💡 Result:

Summary — Vite public directory (static assets)

- Purpose: place files that should be served/copied as-is (robots.txt, favicons, executables) or must keep exact filenames (no hashing). [1][2]
- Location: defaults to <project-root>/public. Configurable with the publicDir option (string | false). [2]
- Dev vs build: served at root (/) in dev and copied to the dist root during build without transforms or hashing. Reference them with a root-absolute path (e.g. /icon.png). [1][2]
- Import behavior: assets in public cannot be imported from JS/CSS. To get hashed/optimized URLs you must import the asset from source (e.g. import img from './img.png'). [1][3]
- Notes: set the Vite base option when deploying to a subpath so absolute public paths resolve correctly. [3]

Sources: Vite docs — Static Asset Handling and config (publicDir). [1][2][3]

---

🌐 Web query:

`Storybook Vite static directories configuration publicDir`

💡 Result:

Short answer: Use Storybook's staticDirs in .storybook/main.js|ts for static assets (served at /path), and — if you need Vite's publicDir behavior — set Vite's publicDir inside the Vite config that Storybook uses (via core.builder.viteConfigPath or viteFinal). Example patterns:

1) Simple Storybook staticDirs (recommended for Storybook-only assets)
- .storybook/main.ts
  - staticDirs: ['../public', '../static']
  - or object form: staticDirs: [{ from: '../my-assets', to: '/assets' }].
(Storybook serves files at the given "to" path; reference assets with absolute paths like /image.png). [1][2]

2) If you need Vite's publicDir (serve/copy as Vite does), set publicDir in Vite config and tell Storybook to use it:
- Option A — point Storybook to a custom Vite config:
  - core: { builder: { name: '@storybook/builder-vite', options: { viteConfigPath: '../vite.config.js' } } }
  - In ../vite.config.js export defineConfig({ publicDir: 'public-vite' })
- Option B — modify Vite config via viteFinal in .storybook/main.ts:
  - async viteFinal(config) { config.publicDir = path.resolve(__dirname, '../public-vite'); return config; }
This uses Vite's publicDir semantics (served at / and copied to dist) so assets behave like Vite's public directory. [3][2]

References:
- Storybook staticDirs docs. [1]
- Storybook Vite builder / viteFinal docs. [2]
- Vite publicDir docs. [3]

If you want, tell me which behavior you need (Storybook-only staticDirs vs full Vite publicDir) and I’ll give the exact file snippets for your project.

---



</details>

**Add context on how to configure Vite's `publicDir` option in Storybook.**

The technical information is accurate—setting `publicDir: false` does prevent Vite's automatic directory copying. However, readers need clarification on where to apply this configuration. In Storybook, this must be set via `viteFinal` in `.storybook/main.ts` (or the Vite config Storybook uses). Consider extending the callout to include a brief example: `async viteFinal(config) { config.publicDir = false; return config; }` or a link to Storybook's Vite builder documentation.
